doc.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Audiences surprised by Sandke's modern records
summary: Sandke recalls a DJ expecting easy-listening jazz and getting a Kafkaesque 'Lullaby of Broadway' with Ray Anderson and Brecker; he dislikes being pigeon-holed.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Right. I think the one that really threw people for a loop was the record after this, which had Ray Anderson and Michael Brecker. And the first tune on it was “Lullaby of Broadway.” And I know that some, I think it was Jazzbo Collins, you know he got the record, oh Randy Sandke, well this will be a nice kind of like, you know, easy listening jazz, and put it on, and it’s supposed to be this Kafkaesque picture of, you know, New York at rush hour kind of thing. And so he was a little bit thrown for a loop. So that happens sometimes with people encountering my music.
Would you bring in Michael Brecker and that crew and do that at the Aspen festival?

Well I mean it’s not, you know I don’t really hire the people here. But that is one of the, I don’t know, that’s an aspect of jazz today and it’s kind of, sometimes it’s problematical for me because people tend to get labeled and pigeon-holed and I understand that. I think it’s, you know it’s probably a better career move to be identified with one thing. You’re more salable. People know what to expect. But me personally, I have a hard time with that just because of I think the various kind of accidents that sort of formed my personal career, which I mean I can go into now if you want.
